info.title: Tools — smart-base
info.description: The call contracts of the harness's Tools, one operation per Tool, generated from the Tool nodes (`schemas/tools/tool.ts`) so standard API tooling can read them. **No HTTP server serves these paths**: each Tool is reached as its `x-invoke` says — a command line, an MCP tool, or an in-process call. Tags are the skills each Tool satisfies.

post.description: Derive FSH from a DAK's BPMN business processes (the inverse of the extractors).

fsh.description: Generated FSH, for SUSHI to compile.

x-selection.when: An L2 business process is to reach L3 as a computable artefact, not only a picture.
x-selection.limits: Requires a `smart-base` checkout at `SMART_BASE_HOME`; without one the capability is ABSENT, not a clean run.

post.description: Generate `dak-api.html`, the DAK API's entry page, and the per-artefact `.openapi.json` / `.displays.json` sidecars.

x-selection.when: The DAK API is to have a reader-facing entry point.
x-selection.limits: `dak-api.html` links its schemas to a `schemas/` directory that does not hold the root enumeration schemas. Resolve a sidecar from the index, never by composing the hub's path.
x-selection.cost: The largest upstream script; runs inside the publisher container against the full output.

post.description: Derive the DAK configuration from `sushi-config.yaml` plus repository and branch context.

branch.description: Sanitised branch name, for the publication and preview URLs.

x-selection.when: A DAK repository has no configuration yet, or its branch context has changed.
x-selection.limits: Upstream runs it twice, before and after the branch name is sanitised, as an ordering workaround. Run it once, after sanitising.
x-selection.cost: Seconds. The whole DAK phase is gated on the file it writes, so a silent failure disables every later step.

post.description: Render each DMN decision table to an HTML fragment for a page, via `dmn2html.xslt` and `dmn.css`.

html.description: One HTML fragment per decision table.

x-selection.when: A reader needs to see a decision table as a table.
x-selection.limits: Its output is HTML, which the JSON-only render contract (`ig-render-jekyll`) does not accept as a representation. Whether the just-the-docs pipeline gets a structured output from it or carries the HTML as an embedded asset is undecided.

post.description: Generate FHIR `Questionnaire` resources from a DAK's DMN decision tables. Authoring, not rendering: the IG Publisher validates and indexes them like any other resource.

dmnDir.description: The DMN source directory, by convention `input/dmn/`.

questionnaires.description: The generated `Questionnaire` resources, written beside SUSHI's output.

generated.description: How many were produced. Zero means none only when the DMN directory was found; a missing directory is reported as such.

x-selection.when: A DAK carries DMN decision tables and the IG is to expose them as answerable questionnaires.
x-selection.limits: Reads DMN only: a decision expressed only in prose or CQL is skipped without error. It cannot tell an empty DMN directory from a DAK with no decisions.
x-selection.cost: Seconds, no network. It runs before the Publisher, so a failure noticed only downstream costs a build cycle.

post.summary: DAK spreadsheets → DMN, PlanDefinitions, CQL, requirements, logical models
post.description: Run WHO's `extract_dak.py` in a DAK or IG repository. It reads the DAK template spreadsheets (`input/decision-logic/*.xlsx` via `dt_extractor`, `input/system-requirements/*.xlsx` via `req_extractor`, `input/dictionary/*.xlsx` via `dd_extractor`) and the BPMN, and writes DMN decision tables, CPG recommendation PlanDefinitions with citations, CQL library skeletons, Requirements and logical-model FSH. Per the WHO IG Starter Kit (`l3_decisiontables`, `l3_cql`), an adapted decision or scheduling table is an edited copy of the upstream DAK's spreadsheet, never a parallel format.

dakRepository.description: The working directory: a DAK or IG repository with `input/decision-logic/`, `input/system-requirements/` and `input/dictionary/` spreadsheets in the DAK template layout.

dmn.description: Decision tables in the DAK DMN format (namespace `https://www.omg.org/spec/DMN/20240513/MODEL/`), each with an `Annotations` and a `Reference(s)` output.

fsh.description: PlanDefinition, ActivityDefinition, Requirements and logical-model FSH, for SUSHI to compile.

cql.description: CQL library skeletons, one per decision table, with the definitions already present in `input/cql/` carried over.

x-selection.when: An L2 decision-support, scheduling, requirements or data-dictionary component is created or adapted and the upstream DAK keeps it in the WHO DAK spreadsheet template. Look for that spreadsheet upstream before writing a decision table by hand.
x-selection.limits: Reads only the DAK template layout (COVER sheet, per-tab inputs and outputs); a table in any other shape is invisible to it. Requires a `smart-base` checkout at `SMART_BASE_HOME`; without one the capability is ABSENT, not a clean run. Where the upstream DAK repository has its own converters (e.g. `tools/node/processDT*.js` in https://github.com/litlfred/smart-immunizations), use those.
x-selection.cost: Seconds to minutes, no network unless `--run-publisher` is passed.

post.summary: Run the immunization schedule-check app locally on a WHO or country IG
post.description: Start litlfred/awho-mcp's schedule-check web form on this machine: a HAPI FHIR server in Docker, the WHO SMART Immunizations IG loaded, then optionally a country adaptation IG (its decision-logic tables replace WHO's; its country profile is generated from its `input/l2/dependencies.yaml`), the CQL cache warmed, and the form served. Both listen on 127.0.0.1. Unbuilt IGs are built with SUSHI first, and each Library's CQL is embedded from `input/cql/` as the IG Publisher would. A re-run reuses a server loaded from the same commits; `--down` stops both.

who-ig.description: A WHO SMART Immunizations IG checkout, relative to the working directory (the folder holding the checkouts, e.g. `~/space_cats`).

country-ig.description: A country adaptation IG checkout, e.g. `smart-immunizations-uganda`, relative to the working directory. Without it the app follows WHO's own schedule.

down.description: Stop the form and the server.

url.description: The form on 127.0.0.1. It stores nothing; each check is one inline `$apply` round.

x-install.cli: git clone https://github.com/litlfred/awho-mcp && cd awho-mcp && python3 -m pip install -e .

x-selection.when: Trying or demonstrating the immunizations L4 app on a clean IG build, before anything is hosted, on the viewer's own machine.
x-selection.limits: Immunizations only (awho-mcp's catalog is the WHO SMART Immunizations IG). One country per server, because a country IG reuses WHO's PlanDefinition ids. Local only: nothing is published and the URL does not open from another machine.
x-selection.cost: Docker and about 4 GB of memory. First run: the HAPI image pull, about a minute to load and warm, and a SUSHI build of any unbuilt IG. A re-run on the same commits restarts only the form.

post.summary: L1 extraction viewer: a hub and a page per instance with `l1-extraction` directories
post.description: For every visualiser an instance declares with `renderedBy: l1-extraction-pages`, write the hub at `<locale>/<harness>/<id>/` and, with `subgraphs: "instance"`, one page per instance that declares an `l1-extraction` directory. Each page shows, from what the files declare: the L1 statements (graph nodes with a `statement`, and an authored L1 source's `recommendations`); the candidate work list's counts, coverage and decisions; each graph document's nodes by type and edges by predicate (L2 scenario candidates included); counts of curation, mapping, vocabulary, exclusions and run context; and a link from every file to its published copy (cat-harness's `library:viz`), when the site has it, and to its source at the pinned commit. A declared directory not on disk is reported UNKNOWN, never zero.

site.description: The site being built; pages go under it (cat-harness-tools' `visualiser-writers.ts` passes it). Default: the checkout's site directory.

root.description: The checkout whose declarations are read. Default: the checkout holding the working directory.

check.description: Write nothing; exit 1 when a page is stale, missing or orphaned.

pages.description: Pages written: the hub and one per instance.

x-selection.when: Publishing a site that should show what each L1 extraction holds.
x-selection.limits: Validates nothing (`l1-recommendation-candidates` and `l1-recommendation-scenarios` do, on every write) and does not re-render the JSON-LD (the library viewer publishes it).
x-selection.cost: Reads each file of each declared directory once.

post.description: Find every normative sentence of an ingested `library/` entry (folio-assistant-core's `l1-coverage` markers), flag uncertain readings, and propose the publication's identity. Given an agent's `l1-recommendation-curation/v1`, refuse a non-verbatim statement or an unknown location, and write the recommendations and remarks as an L1 3.0 graph (checked with `kg/src/validate.ts`) with coverage and proposed, unsigned exclusions.

curation.description: The agent's decisions per candidate location (`l1-recommendation-curation/v1`). Absent: only the work list is written.

candidates.description: `recommendation-candidates.json` — every normative sentence, its hints and its decision; cites the run context.

graph.description: `l1.json` — L1 3.0 publication, recommendation and remark nodes, every one `inferred`.

exclusions.description: `exclusions.proposed.json`, in `l1-coverage`'s shape; none counts until a person signs it.

warnings.description: `extraction-warnings.md` — undecided candidates, unsigned exclusions, statements taken from a layout fragment.

x-selection.when: A WHO guideline, position paper or handbook has been ingested and its recommendations are to become L1 3.0 nodes — especially one with no `Recommendation N:` labels, where `extract-smart-kg-l1` finds none.
x-selection.limits: Finds candidates by marker words only: a recommendation without `should`/`must`/`recommend…` (a table step, an imperative) is invisible to it. The splitter reads a bulleted list or table row as one sentence; the curation's `statement` override narrows it. It decides nothing: with no curation every candidate is `undecided`.

post.description: From an agent's `l1-scenario-mapping/v1`, write one smart-kg L2 `user-scenario` candidate per L1 recommendation, joined to a `persona` and a `business-process` by smart-kg L2's existing edges. Reuses the guide's own personas and processes, then smart-base's generic `DAK.Persona.*`; otherwise a glossary candidate or `could-not-determine`, each with a WARNING. Never invents a process.

l1.description: The recommendations: `l1-recommendation-candidates`' L1 3.0 graph, or an authored L1 YAML.

vocabulary.description: The target guide's personas and processes (`l1-scenario-vocabulary/v1`).

mapping.description: The agent's persona, process, act, outcome and domain per recommendation, each with a source and a basis.

warnings.description: `scenario-warnings.md` — processes not determined, personas that are glossary candidates.

x-selection.when: Each extracted recommendation is to say who acts on it and during which business process, before any L2 asset is drawn.
x-selection.limits: Checks ids against the vocabulary and coverage against the recommendations. Whether a persona or process is the RIGHT one is the agent's judgement, and stays `candidate` until a person reviews it. smart-kg's `user-scenario` has no slot for domain, link source or review status, so those ride on the edges.

post.description: The smart-base collector for core's `publish-extracted-statements` step: an `l1-extraction` directory's authored L1 sources (`recommendations:` rows) and scenario-candidate graphs (`user-scenario` nodes whose `evidence.location` names a row), written as `folio-extracted-statements/v1` lists, each statement with the library entry its L1 source names and the page it was read from. Core's `statements:pages` then renders them with links to the entry and section.

instance-root.description: The instance the evidence locations are relative to; the working directory when absent.

check.description: Compare instead of writing: exit 1 when a list is stale.

lists.description: `<stem>.recommendations.json` per L1 source and `<stem>.scenarios.json` per scenario graph.

x-selection.when: An L1 extraction's statements are to be published, with links to their sources, in the folio's own pages and the shared viewer.
x-selection.limits: An L1 source that names no library entry is refused. A row's page is its first page. A node citing a file that is not an L1 source (a persona citing the mapping) is not a statement and is skipped.

post.summary: Authored L1 → verbatim against transcriptions and image narratives
post.description: Check authored L1 (`*.l1.yaml`, the measles pattern) for a source with no usable text layer: each statement must be verbatim in the image narrative (`images.json`) or the `transcription` block it names; every transcription word (digits aside) must be corroborated by the entry's text layer unless listed under `inspectionOnly`; keys must be unique.

dir.description: The directory of authored `*.l1.yaml`; each names its library entry in `graph.source.entry`.

report.description: One summary line per file and one `FINDING` line per failure. Exit 0 clean, 1 findings, 2 nothing to check (not a pass).

x-selection.when: The L1 was authored from inspected images or transcriptions because `l1-recommendation-candidates` found no normative sentence in the entry's text layer (a poster, a slide deck).
x-selection.limits: Verbatim is checked after NFKC normalisation with private-use glyphs dropped, so digits a text layer maps to private-use code points rest on inspection alone. Whether the transcription reads the picture correctly is the reviewer's call (`bun run cat narratives`).

post.summary: Seed the FHIR package cache, with WHO's published site as a source
post.description: Run fhir-harness's `fhir-cache-seed-npm` with smart-base's publisher-site rules (`SMART_PUBLISHER_SITE_REPOS`), so `smart.who.int.*` packages can also be read from WHO's published-site repository, each fetch verified against the tarball's own package.json. All other sources and checks are the seeder's.

sushi-config.description: Seed what this IG pins: its `dependencies:` and the core package for its `fhirVersion`.

cache.description: Default `~/.fhir/packages`, which SUSHI and the IG Publisher read.

missing.description: Exit 1 when any is missing, each listed with why.

x-selection.when: Seeding the cache for a WHO SMART IG where packages.fhir.org is unreachable.
x-selection.limits: The site rule only adds a source; the seeder's trust checks, exact-version rule and missing list are unchanged.
x-selection.cost: As `fhir-cache-seed-npm`, plus one `git ls-remote` and one download per `smart.who.int.*` package.

post.description: Scan the Publisher's `output/` for `{ResourceType}-{id}.json` and emit a Liquid include assigning `smart__<ResourceType>__<id>__<category>__<key>` for each published resource.

igOutput.description: The Publisher's `output/`, the script's source of truth.

igRoot.description: Repository root, where `input/` lives. Defaults to `.`.

x-selection.when: Page content needs to reference a published resource by canonical URL, page URL, download URL or display label without hard-coding it.
x-selection.limits: The documentation page it writes, `input/pagecontent/smart.liquid.md`, is only processed by the NEXT build, so the script also writes `output/smart.liquid.html` directly; a surface that takes two builds to converge cannot support an incremental staging loop. Ids are normalised by replacing every non-alphanumeric character with `_`, so ids differing only in punctuation collide into one variable.
x-selection.cost: Seconds. Recomputed from scratch on every run; no delta path.

post.description: Look up a concept or code token for a semantic slot across the four reuse-first rungs of the `terminology-coding` methodology: (1) the target guide's `l1-scenario-vocabulary/v1`; (2) smart-base's generic personas (`DAK.Persona.*`), GRADE `code-lists/*.json` and the `guideline-domain` SKOS glossary; (3) local WHO/ILO FSH CodeSystems (`ISCO08`, `CDHIv2`, `CDHIv1`, `CDSCv2`, `KGTerminologySystem`); (4) a proposed `glossary-terms` candidate (`status: "candidate"`), or `could-not-determine` for `business-process`.

query.description: The term, identifier or code token to look up.

vocabulary.description: The target guide's personas and business processes (`l1-scenario-vocabulary/v1`), rung 1.

out.description: Where to write the result JSON.

x-selection.when: Coding L1 narrative statements or L2 DAK slots (personas, processes, domains, interventions, conditions, medicines, GRADE ratings) reuse-first, per `terminology-coding`.
x-selection.limits: Queries local code lists, SKOS glossaries, `l1-scenario-vocabulary/v1` files and FSH CodeSystems, offline. It ranks lexical exact and close matches only and prepares rung-4 candidate records; semantic fit and exclusion sign-off stay human judgements in `classify-and-code-content.bpmn`.

Count.description: A non-negative count — how many of something, or how many to show. Zero is a real answer.

DocId.description: A library document id, e.g. WPR-RDO-2020-003-eng

FilesystemPath.description: A filesystem path, possibly outside the repository. Not admissible as a command-line argument.

Flag.description: A boolean switch — projects to a bare flag, with no value word

Port.description: TCP port for a locally bound server; 0 asks the OS for a free one.

RepoPath.description: A path relative to the repository root. No `..` segments.

skill.classify-and-code-content.input.title: Classify and Code Content Input
skill.classify-and-code-content.input.description: Slot, query token, and optional target-guide or generic vocabulary paths for reuse-first terminology lookup and content coding.

slot.description: The semantic slot being classified and coded, determining the authoritative scheme and reuse-first ladder.

query.description: The concept term, identifier, or code token to look up across the reuse-first precedence rungs.

vocabulary.description: Optional repository path to the target guide's personas and business processes (l1-scenario-vocabulary/v1), Rung 1 of reuse.

generic.description: Optional repository path to smart-base's generic personas (l1-scenario-vocabulary/v1), Rung 2 of reuse.

scheme.description: Optional scheme identifier filter (e.g. guideline-domain, ISCO08, CDHIv2, grade-recommendation-strength).

out.description: Optional repository path where the lookup result JSON is written.

skill.classify-and-code-content.output.title: Classify and Code Content Output
skill.classify-and-code-content.output.description: Ranked terminology lookup hits across the four reuse-first rungs, best SKOS match kind, and either the resolved coding or the candidate/warning to record.

slot.description: The semantic slot that was queried.

query.description: The query token or concept label that was looked up.

bestMatchKind.description: SKOS mapping precision of the top hit across local and base vocabularies, or none when Rung 4 applies.

selectedRung.description: The reuse-first precedence rung that settled the lookup.

candidateToMint.description: Populated when bestMatchKind is none: either a glossary-terms candidate entry (status: candidate) or could-not-determine for business-process, with its greppable WARNING line.

skill.recommendation-candidates.input.title: Recommendation Candidates Input
skill.recommendation-candidates.input.description: One ingested L1 source to turn into L1 3.0 recommendation nodes. Step 1 of recommendation-extraction, run once per included source.

entry.description: An ingested library/<id>/ with page-tagged sections/*.md and structure.json.

curation.description: The agent's decision per candidate location (l1-recommendation-curation/v1). Absent: only the work list is written.

skill.recommendation-candidates.output.title: Recommendation Candidates Output
skill.recommendation-candidates.output.description: The work list and, once curated, the L1 3.0 graph of one source.

candidates.description: recommendation-candidates.json: every normative sentence, its hints and its decision.

graph.description: l1.json: the L1 3.0 publication, recommendation and remark nodes, every one inferred. Present once a curation is given.

exclusions.description: exclusions.proposed.json, in l1-coverage's shape; none counts until a person signs it.

warnings.description: extraction-warnings.md: undecided candidates, unsigned exclusions, statements from a layout fragment.

skill.recommendation-scenarios.input.title: Recommendation Scenarios Input
skill.recommendation-scenarios.input.description: The L1 recommendations of one source, and what to join them to. Step 2 of recommendation-extraction.

l1.description: The recommendations: recommendation-candidates' L1 3.0 graph, or an authored L1 YAML.

vocabulary.description: The target guide's personas and processes (l1-scenario-vocabulary/v1).

generic.description: smart-base's generic personas, the second rung of reuse.

mapping.description: The agent's persona, process, act, outcome and domain per recommendation, each with a source and a basis.

skill.recommendation-scenarios.output.title: Recommendation Scenarios Output
skill.recommendation-scenarios.output.description: One smart-kg L2 user-scenario candidate per L1 recommendation.

warnings.description: scenario-warnings.md: processes not determined, personas that are glossary candidates.

skill.transcription-verbatim.input.title: Transcription Verbatim Input
skill.transcription-verbatim.input.description: Authored L1 for a source with no usable text layer (a poster, a slide deck), to check against the image narratives and transcriptions it names. A step of recommendation-extraction, run when recommendation-candidates found no normative sentence in the entry's text layer.

dir.description: The directory of authored *.l1.yaml; each names its library entry in graph.source.entry.

skill.transcription-verbatim.output.title: Transcription Verbatim Output
skill.transcription-verbatim.output.description: The verdict on each authored L1 file: every statement verbatim in the image narrative or transcription it names, every transcription word corroborated by the text layer unless listed under inspectionOnly, and unique keys.

report.description: One summary line per file and one FINDING line per failure. Exit 0 clean, 1 findings, 2 nothing to check (not a pass).

Text.description: A short single-line human string. Not admissible as a command-line argument.
